note: The parts index: every part an RV is made of, by system, with what it does, how it fails, which RV types have it, which of our guides already covers it, and the phrasings a reader would search. Built 2026-09-29 from Ty's list plus the 110 component makers already catalogued in _data/manuals.json. No models, no specs: this is the index that tells us what content to research next. Each part also carries `makers`: the manufacturers already catalogued in the manuals directory whose documentation covers it, with the archive URL. 18 of 210 parts have a source waiting before any research starts, and a part with makers and no guide is the cheapest content on this list. A ninth system, propane, was added after a completeness check against the manuals taxonomy found the supply side of every gas appliance missing: the furnace and water heater were indexed, and the tank, regulator, hoses and detector feeding them were not. A demand run must MERGE its results rather than write the file back from memory: the first run read _data/parts.json, spent ten minutes measuring, then wrote its in-memory copy over the propane system added while it ran. 2026-10-15 completeness pass: 54 parts added against the five coach types and both ends of the market (satellite TV, Starlink, TV mounts and lifts, dishwasher, washer and dryer split apart, compartment locks and keys, toy hauler ramp door and fuel station, pop-up lift and canvas, and the class A systems: hydronic heat, heated floors, power and hose reels, air leveling, basement air), and `motorhome` split into `class-a` and `class-c` so the type chips say which coach a part belongs to.

quotes.quote: The heat pump will shut down at conditions which would cause outdoor coil freeze-up, generally near freezing temperatures.

Auxiliary heat operation will be activated when the measured temperature of the outdoor temperature sensor is less than 30 °F (-1 °C). ... Auxiliary heat operation will be de-activated and the heat pump operation will resume when the temperature of the outdoor temperature sensor is higher than 35 °F (2 °C).
The Coleman-Mach heat pump is an effective heat source, as long as outdoor temperatures are above 45°F.

The heat pump will operate on reverse refrigerant cycle while heating at outdoor temperatures above approximately 40 degrees F. When the outdoor temperature is below approximately 40 degrees F, the heat pump compressor will shut down to prevent outdoor coil freeze-up.

evidence.note: Coleman's own documents disagree: the 1976-299 manual shuts the compressor down at about 40 F, the 1976-529 manual at about freezing, and the FAQ says to heat with the furnace below 45 F. The card gives each maker's cutoff rather than one universal figure.
